history_policy: This version hash-inherits every V12 workload, mode, jobs, checksum, timing boundary, engine-availability, acceptance, allocation, GC-pause, CPU, and resident-memory decision. It versions successful/failed tier-up and deoptimization latency and removes the completed issue-461 metric panel; any later workload, boundary, jobs, checksum, metric, or acceptance change creates another version.
change: Adds successful and failed baseline/optimizer tier-up attempt counts, total/max nanoseconds from accepted compilation claim through publication outcome, and deoptimization total/max nanoseconds from a recoverable native exit through fully reconstructed interpreter continuation. Native execution before the exit is excluded, ordinary contexts perform no timing queries, and the issue-461 metric inventory is complete.

tier_attribution.scope: one fresh zig-js process and context per workload and structural variant; all attribution remains opt-in and outside scored timing rows
tier_attribution.invocation: one inherited full-work call with the frozen jobs and lane-zero input; retained RSS is sampled after its host checkpoint and before Context destruction
tier_attribution.equivalence: For warmup and invocation independently, each base/variant pair must select the same non-empty set of tree-walker, VM, baseline, optimizer, optimizer-OSR, and deoptimization paths and allocate exactly the same number of environments. Exact tier, timing, runtime, synchronization, allocation, GC-pause, process CPU, resident-memory, and worker values remain visible rather than normalized away; every Wasm workload must record an invocation-phase Wasm dispatch.
tier_attribution.timing_isolation: Attribution uses fresh opt-in processes and contexts outside every scored timing row; ordinary contexts retain a null execution-attribution pointer and therefore perform no tier-up, deoptimization, or process-resource clock queries.

recognizer_audit.prohibited: Every representative workload identifier is absent from engine source. Identifiers exist only in the owned workload, manifest, and benchmark tooling.
